observations.problem: Registered bridge decks are painted in the city contact raster below animated inland water and disappear at runtime.
Station footprint, rail terminal, bank material, and water edge do not share a coherent contact plane; stray source fragments remain visible.
Generic infrastructure-atlas tiles fill node apertures with repeated circular plazas and disconnected road fragments, making buildings read as stickers.
City source and node contact pixels extend beyond supported terrain into the coast; plaza depth and ridge depth conflict.

observations.region: open coastal water north and east of the capital
observations.problem: Large city/source silhouettes leak into open water because the selected source mask permits district-wide off-terrain overhangs.

observations.region: mountain tunnel and south-southeast rail approach
observations.problem: Rail cells have hard terrain contacts, inconsistent grade transitions, and insufficient terrain closure at tunnel and viaduct joins.
Station visual anchor, foreground track, and authored rail centerline do not yet read as one terminal at close zoom.

observations.region: capital-wide roads, retaining walls, and building entries
observations.problem: Road continuity is obscured by duplicate underlay tiles and some independent buildings lack a clean substrate-to-entry transition.
Building, substrate, rail, and water fidelity and opacity transitions must be validated together after placement is stable.
The Go building's visible drainage language has no believable receiving water body at its current socket.
observations.candidateCorrection: Evaluate swapping the two highlighted nodes or move Go to a terrain-supported river-adjacent socket with a downstream outfall, intact road access, and safe shoreline setback.

observations.problem: The terrain canvas redraws all visible site tiles at settled 2x resolution for every camera commit, producing one long task per pan step. Animated building decoders and both continuous water loops add secondary motion-time pressure.

measuredBaseline.workload: 40 alternating camera commits at 50ms intervals in site tier

observations.acceptedCorrection: Render resident capital LOD while the camera is moving, present site tiles once after a 180ms settle, use static building posters during motion, and suspend continuous water animation while view uniforms change.

observations.region: river banks and building contact pads
observations.problem: The ready runtime still mounts city-node-environment-detail-r1 above live inland water plus a transparent compatibility raster. Rock, path, and plaza fragments from the stale plate visibly cross water and duplicate concept substrate material.

observations.region: all four registered city river crossings
observations.problem: Concept-source fragments passed alpha coverage checks but did not read as bridges in the live render. Every crossing needs an independent, alpha-clean bridge asset centered on the frozen registered socket with land-supported endpoints and visible over-water structure.
observations.acceptedCorrection: Replace source-derived crossing fragments with four independent bridge sprites; preserve the existing landmark centers and validate water overlap, endpoint support, source hashes, and live composition.

observations.region: station, both mountain portals, viaduct, and south-southeast rail exit
observations.problem: Rail sprites overlap numerically but their rails, sleepers, curves, viaduct transitions, station approach, and tunnel entries do not form a believable continuous railway. The current validation permits rail-gauge drift and visible disconnections.
observations.acceptedCorrection: Define one explicit train centerline and swept train envelope, place every authored rail segment from that authority, bind the moving train to the same path, and fail generation on centerline gaps, tangent discontinuities, gauge drift, unsupported spans, or station/portal clearance violations.

observations.region: station-side and south mountain tunnel portals
observations.problem: The tunnel apertures are small terrain holes without credible stone portal faces, wing walls, retaining masonry, ballast transition, or clearance for the train envelope.
observations.acceptedCorrection: Author full masonry portal structures around train-envelope-sized openings, add wing walls and terrain occlusion, continue rails and ballast into the darkness, and validate back/track/foreground depth order at both ends.

observations.problem: Independent buildings are registered to concept sockets but still read as isolated objects scattered on terrain; district hierarchy, road approach, plaza ownership, retaining transitions, and relation to water and rail are not coherent enough to match the accepted concept direction.
observations.acceptedCorrection: Stabilize the rail and bridge circulation spines first, then perform a controlled placement pass that preserves concept hierarchy while adjusting sockets, scale, road entries, retaining walls, and contact layers as one composition. Revalidate all LODs after placement is locked.
observations.supersedingCorrection: The live render disproved the nineteen-permanent-aperture composition model. Use the coherent concept-derived fabric as the capital-scale authority, retain its roads, terraces, retaining walls, district massing, and baked station, and introduce at most one feathered semantic building replacement at site or close range. The accepted isometric concept controls projection and layout; the alternate oblique concept is massing and circulation evidence only.

observations.region: site and close semantic buildings, population cues, rail, and bridges
observations.problem: The focused independent building is visibly oversized against the coherent concept street module and nearby people. Population height, door and storey height, rail gauge, locomotive clearance, road width, and bridge deck width currently come from separate asset-local scales rather than one world-scale authority.
observations.acceptedCorrection: After circulation placement is stable, define one artboard human-height unit and validate every focused building against door height and storey height, every transport asset against rail gauge and train clearance, and every bridge against believable pedestrian and vehicle width. Apply per-asset registration scale only from those ratios and recheck site and close LODs.
